These shapes are arranged in a pattern.

[Image: Pattern of shapes]

Which set of shapes is arranged in the same pattern?
reference_items.figure_description:
In the stem, a horizontal sequence of shapes shows: 1 open circle, 1 open triangle, 2 open circles, 2 open triangles, 3 open circles, 3 open triangles.
Option A shows a horizontal sequence: 1 solid star, 1 open square, 1 solid star, 1 open square, 2 solid stars, 2 open squares, 2 solid stars, 2 open squares.
Option B shows a horizontal sequence: 1 open square, 1 solid star, 2 open squares, 1 solid star, 3 open squares, 1 solid star, 4 open squares.
Option C shows a horizontal sequence: 1 solid star, 1 open square, 2 solid stars, 2 open squares, 3 solid stars, 3 open squares.
Option D shows a horizontal sequence: 2 open squares, 2 solid stars, 1 open square, 1 solid star, 2 open squares, 2 solid stars, 1 open square, 1 solid star.

options.text: [Image: 6 squares arranged in two offset rows of 3]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four shapes composed of identical square units are shown:
- Option A: A rectangle consisting of a grid with 2 rows and 3 columns (6 square units in total).
- Option B: A horizontal bar consisting of a single row of 6 square units (6 square units in total).
- Option C: A rectangle consisting of a grid with 2 rows and 4 columns (8 square units in total).
- Option D: A figure consisting of 6 square units arranged in two rows of 3 squares: a top row of 3 adjacent squares, and a bottom row of 3 adjacent squares shifted to the right so that its leftmost square is directly beneath the rightmost square of the top row (6 square units in total).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Here is part of a wall chart that lists numbers from 1 to 100.

[Image: Part of a 1 to 100 wall chart]

Below is part of the same wall chart. What number should be in the box with the question mark inside?

[Image: Three boxes containing 43, 53, and ?]
reference_items.figure_description:
The first image shows the top section of a 100-number wall chart organized in 10 columns:
- Row 1 shows numbers 1 through 10 from left to right.
- Row 2 shows numbers 11 through 20 from left to right.
- Row 3 shows numbers 21 through 25 in the first five columns, with the remainder of the chart cut off.

The second image shows three individual square boxes from the chart arranged in a step-down pattern from top-left to bottom-right:
- The top-left box contains the number 43.
- The middle box contains the number 53, shifted down and to the right.
- The third box contains a question mark (?), positioned directly below and adjacent to the right side of the box with 53, sharing its top-left corner with the bottom-right corner of the 53 box.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: four angles varied in size and labeled P, Q, R, and S from left to right.]

In which of the following are the angles ordered by size, from least to greatest?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four angles are shown side by side, labeled from left to right as P, Q, R, and S. Each angle has a horizontal ray pointing to the right, a second ray extending from the left endpoint, and a curved arc indicating the angle between the two rays:
- Angle P is an acute angle opening upward and to the right at approximately 45°.
- Angle Q is an obtuse angle opening upward and to the left at approximately 120°.
- Angle R is a right angle (90°) formed with a vertical ray extending straight up.
- Angle S is an acute angle opening upward and to the right at approximately 30°, smaller than angle P.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
